cards.text: Paul is writing to the church in Corinth. He's just told them his heart is wide open, and he's asked them to open theirs too. Now he gives them a command: "Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers."
Then he backs it up with questions. "For what partnership can righteousness have with wickedness? Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?"

cards.question: Righteousness and wickedness. Light and darkness. Why does Paul put these pairs side by side?

answers.text: They are opposites that don't mix
They work best as a team
They are two names for one thing

cards.text: Paul's stacking up these questions like cookies on a tray, and friend, he is NOT slowing down. Next he asks what harmony there is between Christ and Belial.

cards.question: Paul asks what harmony there is between Christ and Belial. True or false: he's pairing them as partners who work together.

cards.text: He asks what a believer has in common with an unbeliever. Then one more: what agreement can there be between the temple of God and idols?

cards.question: Then Paul says something surprising. What does he say is the temple of the living God?

cards.text: WE are the temple, friend. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and nobody ever looked in there and said, "Ooh, I could LIVE here."

cards.question: Paul backs it up with what God has said. True or false: God promises to dwell with His people and walk among them.

cards.text: God's words keep going: "I will be their God, and they will be My people." And the next line from the Lord starts with "Therefore."

cards.question: After that "Therefore," what does the Lord call His people to do?

answers.text: Come out from among them and be separate
Stay right where they are and fit in
Build Him a new house made of stone

cards.question: The Lord also says to touch no unclean thing. True or false: He promises He will receive them.

cards.text: Then Paul quotes the Lord Almighty one more time. And friend, this promise gets even closer than a temple.

cards.question: What does the Lord Almighty say He will be to His people?
And the Lord Almighty says they will be His ___ and ___.

cards.text: Friend, I got picked out of a closing-sale bin for 25 cents. And the Lord Almighty is out here calling people His sons and daughters? I need to sit down on my gold base for a second.
So Paul wraps it up, and he calls them beloved. Since we have these promises, he says, let's get cleaned up.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says to cleanse ourselves only from what defiles the body.
Paul says that as we cleanse ourselves, we're perfecting ___ in the fear of God.

findings.problem: This story card is only a reaction joke. It tells nothing new from 6:16, because 'we are the temple' was already the answer on card 7, so it doesn't move the baker forward through the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This story card is only a reaction joke. It tells nothing new from 6:18, because 'sons and daughters' was already the answer on card 15. It cites 2 Corinthians 6:18 but tells no part of it.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The setup line 'this promise gets even closer than a temple' points toward a close relationship. That steers the baker to 'A Father' on card 14 and rules out 'A King' and 'A Judge'. It is also a judgment the text never makes.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer is the BSB wording ('Come out from among them and be separate'). 'Stay right where they are and fit in' sounds modern. The right answer sounds more like the Bible than the others, so it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Belial is named here for the first time, and the walkthrough never says who Belial is. Card 5 then asks about Christ and Belial. The text itself doesn't identify Belial, and the common reading (Satan, or worthlessness) comes from outside the passage.
findings.question: Does Belial count as a new person who must be introduced on the card (papa-dorin.md 'New people'), or as a hard word left to the dictionary pop-up (prep-walkthrough.md 'What bite-sized means') because the text leaves Belial unexplained?
